prerequisites.why: The definition of a cyclotomic spectrum by a Frobenius to the Tate construction, the Tate orbit lemma, the formula TC = fib(can − φ) for bounded below objects, the Tate diagonal, and the calculation of THH(F_p) as τ_{≥0}(Z^{tC_p}). Every construction in Sections 2 and 3 is phrased in that language, and Appendix A generalises its Tate diagonal.

prerequisites.citation: Bjørn Ian Dundas, Thomas G. Goodwillie and Randy McCarthy, The local structure of algebraic K-theory, Algebra and Applications 18, Springer (2013)
prerequisites.why: The theorem that the cyclotomic trace induces an equivalence K(R, I) ≃ TC(R, I) for a nilpotent ideal. It is what turns every TC statement in this paper into a K-theory statement, together with Clausen–Mathew–Morrow's henselian version.

prerequisites.citation: Thomas G. Goodwillie, Relative algebraic K-theory and cyclic homology, Ann. of Math. 124 (1986), 347–402
prerequisites.why: The rational theorem K(R, I) ≃ HC^-(R, I) for a nilpotent ideal in a Q-algebra, which the Beilinson fibre square is the p-adic refinement of; the paper's Theorem A is its p-adic analogue.

prerequisites.citation: Spencer Bloch, Hélène Esnault and Moritz Kerz, p-adic deformation of algebraic cycle classes, Invent. Math. 195 (2014), 673–722
prerequisites.why: The theorem reproved and extended in Section 4: a class in K_0 of the special fibre of a proper smooth p-adic formal scheme lifts to continuous K-theory exactly when its crystalline Chern character lies in the Hodge filtration. Nothing in the atlas plans it or the p-adic variational Hodge conjecture it is aimed at.

prerequisites.citation: Alexander Beilinson, Relative continuous K-theory and cyclic homology, Münster J. Math. 7 (2014), 51–81
prerequisites.why: The obstruction class in de Rham cohomology modulo the Hodge filtration whose vanishing detects a lift to continuous K-theory, and the rational Beilinson fibre square that this paper's Theorem A refines integrally.

prerequisites.citation: Benjamin Antieau, Periodic cyclic homology and derived de Rham cohomology, Ann. K-Theory 4 (2019), 505–519
prerequisites.why: The Hochschild–Kostant–Rosenberg filtrations on HP and HC^- with graded pieces derived de Rham cohomology and its Hodge filtration, which is how the bottom row of the Beilinson square is computed in Sections 4 and 6.

prerequisites.citation: Bhargav Bhatt, p-adic derived de Rham cohomology (2012)
prerequisites.why: p-adic derived de Rham cohomology with its derived Hodge filtration, its agreement with the p-completed de Rham complex for smooth maps, and the divided-power calculations; it is the target of the obstruction class of Theorem E and one side of the comparison of Section 6.

prerequisites.citation: Peter Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, Forum Math. Pi 1 (2013), e1
prerequisites.why: The degeneration of the Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence for proper smooth rigid analytic varieties, quoted in Section 4 for the de Rham cohomology of the generic fibre of a proper smooth formal scheme.

prerequisites.citation: Pierre Berthelot and Arthur Ogus, F-isocrystals and de Rham cohomology I, Invent. Math. 72 (1983), 159–199
prerequisites.why: Theorem 2.4, the rationalised comparison RΓ_dR(X_K/K) ≃ RΓ_crys(X_k; Q_p) ⊗_{K_0} K for a smooth p-adic formal scheme over a ramified O_K, which is how the crystalline Chern character is compared with the Hodge filtration in the ramified case.

prerequisites.citation: Michel Gros, Classes de Chern et classes de cycles en cohomologie de Hodge–Witt logarithmique, Mém. Soc. Math. France 21 (1985)
prerequisites.why: Crystalline Chern classes of vector bundles on a regular scheme of characteristic p with the usual axioms, from which the crystalline Chern character of Section 4 is built; the atlas plans Chern classes in K-theory at SchemeKTheoryOperations S.7 but not their crystalline version.

prerequisites.citation: Thomas Geisser and Lars Hesselholt, On relative and bi-relative algebraic K-theory of rings of finite characteristic, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 24 (2011), 29–49
prerequisites.why: The theorem that relative K-theory of a nilpotent ideal in a ring in which p is nilpotent is torsion, recovered here as a corollary of Theorem C and used for the continuity of continuous K-theory.

prerequisites.citation: Lars Hesselholt and Ib Madsen, On the K-theory of local fields, Ann. of Math. 158 (2003), 1–113
prerequisites.why: The TC-theoretic calculation of the p-adic K-theory of a local field, against which the integral calculations of Section 7 are compared and which they partly reprove; KTheoryFiniteLocalFields L.5 and L.6 plan the calculations in this direction.

prerequisites.citation: Laurent Fargues and Jean-Marc Fontaine, Courbes et fibrés vectoriels en théorie de Hodge p-adique, Astérisque 406 (2018)
prerequisites.why: Theorem 6.2.1, that the graded ring ⊕_{i≥0}B_crys(O_C)^{φ = p^i} is generated in degree one; it is what reduces the identification of the maps in the fundamental exact sequence to weight one.

routes.title: Hochschild, cyclotomic and refined trace methods, Part II: p-adic deformation of K-theory classes
routes.brief: Plan the p-adic deformation of K-theory classes: continuous K-theory of p-adic formal schemes, the obstruction to deforming a class from the special fibre, and the p-adic variational Hodge conjecture of Fontaine and Messing that the obstruction theory is aimed at. The final theorems are Theorem D and Theorem E of Antieau, Mathew, Morrow and Nikolaus. Theorem D (their Theorem 4.9, the theorem of Bloch, Esnault and Kerz): for K a complete discretely valued field of characteristic zero with ring of integers O_K and perfect residue field k of characteristic p, and X → Spf(O_K) a proper smooth p-adic formal scheme, a class x ∈ K_0(X_k; Q_p) lifts to K_0^cts(X; Q_p) if and only if its crystalline Chern character ch_crys(x) ∈ ⊕_i H^{2i}_crys(X_k; Q_p) is carried by the de Rham-to-crystalline comparison into ⊕_i Fil^{≥i}H^{2i}_dR(X_K/K). Theorem E (their Theorem 4.14): for X a qcqs p-adic formal scheme with bounded p-power torsion and x ∈ K_i(X_1; Q), there is a natural class c(x) ∈ ⊕_{r≥0}H^{2r−i}(LΩ_X/LΩ_X^{≥r})_{Q_p} vanishing exactly when x lifts to K_i^cts(X; Q), and more precisely a natural equivalence cofib(K^cts(X; Q) → K(X_1; Q)) ≃ ⊕_{r≥0}(LΩ_X/LΩ_X^{≥r}[2r])_{Q_p} in terms of p-adic derived de Rham cohomology with its derived Hodge filtration. The roadmap must cover: continuous invariants F^cts(X) = lim_n F(X_n) of a p-adic formal scheme for F = K, THH, HH, HC^-, HP, TC, with the continuity theorems saying which comparison maps F(X) → F^cts(X) are p-adic equivalences and the warning that for K and a proper scheme this is expected to fail; the crystalline Chern character of a regular scheme of characteristic p, with its Chern classes and the usual axioms; the de Rham cohomology of a smooth p-adic formal scheme with its Hodge filtration, and Berthelot–Ogus's rationalised comparison with the crystalline cohomology of the special fibre; the stacked fibre squares relating K^cts, TC^cts, HC^{-,cts} and HP^cts of a smooth formal O_K-scheme; the Hochschild–Kostant–Rosenberg splitting of HP^cts and HC^{-,cts} into de Rham cohomology and its Hodge filtration, and the resulting p-adic Chern character map, together with the proof that it depends only on the special fibre and is the crystalline Chern character up to a scalar λ^i; Beilinson's obstruction in the proper smooth case and its generalisation, Theorem E; and the statement of the p-adic variational Hodge conjecture itself, recorded as a conjecture with its exact hypotheses and not as a theorem. Import, and do not re-plan: the Beilinson fibre square, the quasi-isogeny comparison of cyclotomic spectra and the p-adic Chern character tr_crys from Hochschild, cyclotomic and refined trace methods (RefinedTraceMethods), stage RT.3b, of which this paper is also the source; the cyclotomic trace, the Dundas–Goodwillie–McCarthy theorem and the Clausen–Mathew–Morrow comparison K(R,(p);Z_p) ≃ TC(R,(p);Z_p) for a ring henselian along (p) from RT.3; Hochschild, cyclic, negative cyclic and periodic cyclic homology with the SBI sequence from RT.1; THH, TC^-, TP and TC from RT.2; and the motivic filtration on TC with its graded pieces from RT.6. Import relative and nonconnective K-theory from General algebraic K-theory (GeneralAlgebraicKTheory), stages K.5 and K.6, and Chern classes, the Chern character and the γ-filtration from K-theory of schemes, localisation and operations (SchemeKTheoryOperations), stage S.7. Import the cotangent complex and its derived exterior powers from Derived de Rham cohomology and its algebraic foundations (DerivedDeRhamCohomology), stage DD.0, derived completion from DD.1, derived de Rham cohomology with its Hodge filtration from DD.2, and the crystalline comparison from DD.4. Import crystalline cohomology, its sites and crystals from Crystalline cohomology, de Rham–Witt and logarithmic foundations (CrystallineCohomology), stages CR.0 and CR.1, and the rational crystalline comparison for a smooth proper formal O_K-model from Cohomology comparisons (CohomologyComparisons), stage CP.2. Record with the statement of the p-adic variational Hodge conjecture that it is open, and that Motives and algebraic cycles (MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles) stage MC.7 owns the register of cycle conjectures and their proved cases, so that the conjecture is cross-referenced there rather than restated. The roadmap owns, and must plan itself, continuous K-theory and the other continuous invariants of a formal scheme, the crystalline Chern character, the identification of the trace-theoretic Chern character with it, and the two obstruction theorems.
routes.reason: Section 4 of the paper is a self-contained body of mathematics that the atlas heads towards nowhere: continuous K-theory K^cts(X) = lim_n K(X_n) of a p-adic formal scheme and the other continuous trace invariants, the crystalline Chern character, the identification of the trace-theoretic Chern character with it, Beilinson's obstruction class, its generalisation to arbitrary qcqs formal schemes with derived de Rham cohomology in place of de Rham cohomology, the Bloch–Esnault–Kerz theorem, and the statement of the p-adic variational Hodge conjecture. A search of the layer descriptions finds no 'continuous K-theory', no 'Bloch–Esnault–Kerz' and no 'variational Hodge'; MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles MC.7 plans a register of cycle conjectures but names only the Hodge, Tate and standard conjectures and the Bloch–Beilinson filtration, and it plans none of the K-theoretic machinery in which the p-adic conjecture is posed. These are new layers in the direction RefinedTraceMethods already goes: they are the application for which the Beilinson fibre square of RT.3b was proved, they use RT.1's cyclic homology, RT.2's THH and TC, RT.3's cyclotomic trace and Clausen–Mathew–Morrow comparison and RT.3b's square as their entire machinery, and RT's own summary calls it a shared trace-theoretic library whose arithmetic applications live in its consumers. So this is a Part II of RefinedTraceMethods rather than a new roadmap. The alternative parent is MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles, whose MC.7 would then acquire the p-adic variational Hodge conjecture and its deformation theory; a reviewer who prefers that should say so, and the brief transfers with the imports reversed. The case for RefinedTraceMethods is that everything here is proved by trace methods and that the only statement about cycles is the conjecture itself, which the brief instructs the design job to cross-reference to MC.7 rather than restate.

RT.3b already exists for this paper: it is titled 'The Beilinson square and the prismatic F-crystal proof bridge' and instructs the blueprint to prove Antieau–Mathew–Morrow–Nikolaus Theorem 2.12 and Corollary 3.9, to supply the quasi-isogeny comparison of their Section 3, to prove the shift dictionary fib(TC(R;Q_p)→TC(R/p;Q_p)) ≃ ΣHC(R;Q_p), and to export the filtered refinement of their Theorem 6.17 that PrismaticCohomology PR.7 uses. Those four statements are therefore planned; what is not planned, and what this route supplies, is everything the proof needs. From Section 2: the cyclotomic spectrum Z_{hC_p} and the cofibre sequence Z_{hC_p} → Z^triv → THH(F_p), the Tate vanishing lemma, the cartesian square of cyclotomic spectra and its TC^-/TP form, the effective bounds on the denominators that give every range of the form 2p − c in the paper, the notion of isogeny and quasi-isogeny, the integral statements Theorem A and Corollary B with their truncation ranges, and the relative statement for a nilpotent ideal. From Section 3, the whole theory of quasi-isogenies of cyclotomic spectra: the TR criterion, the two vanishing criteria, Theorem C on THH of a quasi-isogeny with nilpotent kernel on π_0, its graded, square-zero and augmented cases, and the recovery of Geisser–Hesselholt's theorem. From Section 5, the relative THH over the cyclotomic base S[z] with its filtration and connectivity bounds, and the graded version of the Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze package, which RT.6 owns in its ungraded form. From Section 6, the compatibility of the trace with both filtrations on graded pieces. From Appendix A, the twisted Tate diagonals: the general notion, cyclotomic bases, the criterion on an indexing category, and the graded, filtered and S[z]-linear instances, which is how a graded ring gets a graded cyclotomic structure on its THH — RT.2 constructs the cyclotomic Frobenius in spectra and nothing plans this. The route also names the four planned statements above and the two Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze statements of Section 5 that RT.6 owns, because this paper is their designated source.

PR.4 owns the syntomic complexes: it constructs the syntomic and Tate-twist fibres from the Nygaard pieces and the divided Frobenius with the intrinsic twists, proves the truncation and nearby-cycle and logarithmic de Rham–Witt comparisons, and states that its syntomic realization is shared with RT's TC graded pieces; PR.3 owns the Nygaard filtration, the divided Frobenius and the Breuil–Kisin twists. Sections 5 and 6 of this paper prove what those layers need and do not plan. The structural theorems are the connectivity bound Z_p(i)(R) ∈ D^{≤i+1}(Z_p), sharpened to D^{≤i} for w-strictly local rings, with its consequence that Fil^{≥i}TC(R;Z_p) is (i−1)-connective; the left Kan extension of Z_p(i) and of the motivic filtration from finitely generated p-complete polynomial algebras, hence their definition on all simplicial commutative rings; and the rigidity theorem, that fib(Z_p(i)(R) → Z_p(i)(R/I)) ∈ D^{≤i}(Z_p) for a henselian pair of p-complete rings. The route also carries their whole proof: the connectivity bounds on the Nygaard graded pieces and quotients, the I-adic filtrations modulo p and the nilpotence of the Frobenius on them, the finite-level description of F_p(i), the criteria for being left Kan extended, the continuity statement, and the graded connectivity lemma. Section 6 then supplies the comparison the layer most needs: the Fontaine–Messing description Z_p(i)(R) ≃ fib(φ/p^i − id : LΩ_R^{≥i} → LΩ_R) for i ≤ p−2 and its rational form for all i, with the divisibility of the Frobenius on the Hodge filtration that makes the definition possible, the identification of the image of χ_i with a Frobenius eigenspace, the rigidity of the Frobenius action that pins the comparison down up to a scalar, and the resulting de Rham description of TC(R; Q_p). The computation of the syntomic complexes of a complete discrete valuation ring belongs with them.

E5:animation constructs animated commutative algebras from simplicial commutative rings, polynomial resolutions and sifted left Kan extensions, and E3 proves the left Kan extension theorem with its pointwise formula, uniqueness and cofinality. Appendix B of this paper proves four statements in that range which neither plans: the Frobenius factorisation for a simplicial commutative F_p-algebra, giving natural maps R → R ⊗^L_Z F_p → R whose composites are the Frobenius in both orders; the consequence that a natural transformation defined after base change along Z → F_p descends, after multiplication by p^i, whenever the Frobenius acts by p^i on the source — the device that produces the comparison map χ_i of Section 6 with a controlled denominator; the finiteness classes of almost finitely presented simplicial commutative algebras over a field and over O_K; and the comparison saying that a natural transformation of functors of formally smooth O_K-algebras that depends only on the special fibre descends to a transformation of functors of smooth k-algebras, which is the step that identifies the trace-theoretic Chern character with the crystalline one.

L.6 plans the local higher K-groups — for a finite extension L of Q_p the rank [L:Q_p] of K_{2j−1}(L; Z_p) for j ≥ 2 and the identification of the torsion by Galois cohomology — and L.5 the THH/TR/TC calculations for perfect fields, truncated polynomial rings and complete DVRs that the Hesselholt–Madsen route needs. Section 7 of this paper computes the same groups integrally in the range the effective bounds of Section 2 allow, without those calculations: from the integral Beilinson fibre sequence it obtains K_i(W(k); Z_p) ≅ W(k) for i odd and 0 for i even in the range 1 ≤ i ≤ 2p−5, independently of Bökstedt–Madsen and Rognes, and in the ramified case five-term exact sequences relating K_*(O_F; Z_p) to the Witt-vector groups W_{se}(k)/V_eW_s(k) for 2 ≤ s ≤ p−2, which read the other way give information about the low-degree étale cohomology of F. Both belong inside those layers as a second, trace-light route to their calculations.

R06.1 constructs B_dR^+ with its filtration, B_dR, B_crys^+, B_crys and B_st from the shared A_inf, θ and PD-period maps, and proves their topological, Galois, Frobenius, filtration and monodromy properties. What it does not plan is the fundamental exact sequence relating them: for a perfectoid ring R and i > 0 the pullback square with rows RΓ_proét(Spec(R[1/p]), Q_p(i)) → B_crys(R)^{φ = p^i} and Fil^{≥i}B_dR^+(R) → B_dR^+(R), which for R = O_C is the classical short exact sequence 0 → Q_p(i) → B_crys^{φ=p^i} → B_dR^+/Fil^{≥i} → 0. This paper obtains it as a special case of the Beilinson fibre square on graded pieces, and also supplies the identification of the maps it produces with the classical ones: the restriction to Q_p(1) is the dlog map, a generator maps to a uniformizer of the discrete valuation ring B_dR^+, there is no nonzero Galois-equivariant map C_p → B_dR^+, and Fargues–Fontaine's theorem that ⊕_i B_crys(O_C)^{φ=p^i} is generated in degree one then fixes the higher weights. That compatibility argument is precisely the kind of statement a blueprint has to make explicit.

CP.2 owns the rational crystalline comparison and its descent for a smooth proper formal O_K-model and CP.3 the canonical B_dR^+ deformation of de Rham cohomology with its filtration strictness. The theorem this paper proves in Section 7.3 is their common refinement in the form used by Colmez–Nizioł and Tsuji: for a smooth proper formal O_K-scheme X_0 with base change X to O_C and reduction X̄_0 modulo π, a natural pullback square in D(Q_p) with rows RΓ(X_proét, τ^{≤i}Rψ_*(Q_p(i))) → (A_crys ⊗_{W(k)} RΓ_crys(X̄_0/W(k)))^{φ = p^i}[1/p] and Fil^{≥i}(Ω_{X_0/K} ⊗_K B_dR^+) → (Ω_{X_0/K} ⊗_K B_dR^+). It is the geometric statement that the two layers' maps assemble into, obtained here by descent from the affine syntomic square, and neither layer plans it.

sourceIssues.locator: Example 7.3, the two stated ranges in the computation of the cyclic homology of k over W(k); in arXiv v2, the version read (the published version could not be consulted)
sourceIssues.printed: Using the filtrations of [antieauperiodic], we conclude for i ≤ 2p−1, π_i HC(k/W(k)) ≅ W(k)/p^{s+1} if i = 2s ≥ 0, 0 otherwise. … Thus, in the range 0 ≤ i ≤ 2p−2, we deduce that π_i HC((W(k),(p)/W(k)) ≅ p^{s+1}W(k) if i = 2s, 0 if i is odd.
sourceIssues.correction: The two ranges should be i ≤ 2p−4 and 0 ≤ i ≤ 2p−4 (equivalently i ≤ 2p−3, since the odd groups vanish).
sourceIssues.reason: Both formulas are read off from the sentence immediately before them, that LΩ_k/LΩ_k^{≥s} ≅ W(k)/p^s for s ≤ p−1, applied with s+1 in place of s: π_{2s}HC(k/W(k)) = LΩ_k/LΩ_k^{≥s+1}. That needs s+1 ≤ p−1, i.e. i = 2s ≤ 2p−4. At the first excluded value, i = 2p−2 and s = p−1, the formula would give W(k)/p^p, but LΩ_k here is the p-completed divided power envelope of (p) ⊆ W(k) — that is, W(k) itself — and its Hodge filtration is the divided power filtration, whose p-th step is generated by γ_p(p) = p^p/p!, of p-adic valuation p − 1 since v_p(p!) = 1. So LΩ_k/LΩ_k^{≥p} = W(k)/p^{p−1} and π_{2p−2}HC(k/W(k)) ≅ W(k)/p^{p−1}, not W(k)/p^p; correspondingly the relative group is p^{p−1}W(k), not p^pW(k).
